Rashi on Pesachim 116b:10:1.hebrew: הא הוא דאמר - בסופא דהאי פירקא (דף קכ.), אחד זה ואחד זה דרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 116b:10:1.english: Isn't he the one who said - At the end of this chapter (daf 120a), [he said:] "Both this and that are rabbinic."

Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:1.english: He must lift [it] - When he says, "This matzah that we eat."

Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:2.hebrew: בשר אין מגביה - כשהוא אומר פסח שהיו אבותינו (במצרים) אוכלים, לא יגביה הבשר שהוא זכר לפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:2.english: Meat — one does not lift [it] - When he says, "The Paschal lamb that our ancestors ate (in Egypt)," he should not lift the meat, which is a remembrance of the Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: בשר אינו צריך להגביה, ולא עוד אלא שנראה כמקדיש כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:3.english: This is the reading: "Meat — one does not need to lift [it], and not only that, but [he] appears as one who consecrates [it], etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 116b:7:4.english: One need not raise [the meat] - For he cannot say, "This Paschal offering."

Rashi on Pesachim 116b:9:1.english: Rav Yosef and Rav Sheshet - They were blind.

Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:1:1.hebrew: ואמרתם זבח פסח הוא - פי': באמירה, שצריך לומר "פסח זה שאנו אוכלין". ואיתקש מצה ומרור לפסח, וצ"ל נמי "מצה זו", "מרו' זה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:1:1.english: "And you shall say: It is the sacrifice of the Paschal offering" - Explanation: [This is fulfilled] through speech, for one must say, "This Paschal lamb that we are eating." And matza and maror are equated [in Scripture] to the Paschal lamb, so one must also say, "This matza," [and] "This maror."

Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:4:1.hebrew: לפיכך אנחנו כו' - י"א שבע הודאות ולא יותר, כנגד ז' רקיעים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:4:1.english: "Therefore we," etc. - Some say [there are] seven expressions of thanksgiving and no more, corresponding to the seven heavens.

Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:4:2.hebrew: ה"ג ונאמר לפניו שירה חדשה, וכן נודה לך שיר חדש על גאולתנו - דהכי תניא במכילתא: "כל השירות לשון נקבה, חוץ משירה דלעתיד דלשון זכר", כלומר: שהנקבה יש לה צער לידה, אף כל הנסים יש אחריהם צער, חוץ מלעתיד שאין אחריה צער. וכן יסד הפייט בזולת "אי פתרוס": "שירות אלה לשון נקבה מיוסדים, כי תשועתם כיולדה וגו', תוקף שיר אחרון כזכרים לא יולדים, שירו לה' שיר חדש כו'". וגרסינן שם: "מן הזבחים ומן הפסחים", שחגיגת ארבעה עשר נאכלת קודם לפסח, לפי שהפסח נאכל על השובע:
Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:4:2.english: This is the reading: "And we will say before Him a new song [shirah chadashah]," and similarly, "We will thank You [with] a new song [shir chadash] for our redemption" - For so it was taught in the Mekhilta: "All the songs [in Scripture] are in the feminine gender [shirah], except for the song of the future [redemption], which is in the masculine gender [shir]." That is to say, just as a female experiences the pain of childbirth, so too all miracles have suffering after them, except for [the redemption of] the future, after which there is no suffering. And so did the liturgical poet compose in the zulat [beginning] "Ei Patros": "These songs are formulated in the feminine gender, for their salvation is like a woman in childbirth, etc.; the strength of the final song is like males who do not give birth — 'Sing to the Lord a new song [shir chadash],' etc." And we read there [in that blessing]: "of the [festival] sacrifices and of the Pesach offerings," because the chagigah offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan] is eaten prior to the Pesach offering, since the Pesach offering is eaten when one is [already] sated.

Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:5:1.hebrew: וחותם בגאולה - ת"ק לא פי' כיצד, ופליגי במילתיה ר"ט ור"ע: ר' טרפון אינו חותם בברוך, שלא היה מאריך בדברי בקשה ולא היה אומר אלא הודאה; ור"ע סבר דחותם בה בברוך, לפי שמאריך בדברי בקשה ואומר "כן ה' אלהינו יגיענו כו'". וקי"ל (עירובין דף מו:): הלכה כר' עקיבא מחבירו. וכן מצינו בסנהדרין (דף כא.) גבי "לא ירבה לו נשים", ובריש חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף כח.), דפליגי תנאי במילתיה דתנא קמא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 116b:5:1.english: And one concludes with redemption - The Tanna Kamma did not explain how [one concludes], and Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disagree about his statement: Rabbi Tarfon does not conclude with "Blessed [are You...]," because he would not lengthen [the blessing] with words of supplication, and would only say thanksgiving; whereas Rabbi Akiva holds that one concludes it with "Blessed [are You...]," because he lengthens [it] with words of supplication and says, "So, Lord our God, bring us [to reach...]," etc. And it is established for us (Eruvin 46b) [that] the halakhah follows Rabbi Akiva over his colleague. And similarly we find in Sanhedrin (21a) regarding "he shall not multiply wives for himself," and at the beginning of [the chapter] Chezkath HaBattim (Bava Batra 28a), that Tannaim disagree about the statement of the Tanna Kamma.
